Stop-start

The training only sells when a cohort opens

Your last listed cohort ran 6 October to 13 November 2025 and the page now says “Registration Closed”. Between cohorts, a therapist who wants to learn from you can only join a mailing list.

No first step

Nothing between a follow and $2,400

There’s no low-cost way for a clinician or coach to experience your teaching first. Your self-guided program’s school on Teachable currently shows as offline.

No filter

Nobody is qualified before they enrol

The training is a deposit and checkout; 1:1 work is a request form your team answers by email. You can’t see who is ready, who is a fit, or who needs one more nudge.

Therapists and coaches need grief skills, and you already wrote the books on it. There’s no live moment yet that turns readers in the helping professions into students.

My recommendation

A free live masterclass for helping professionals, Beyond the Five Stages, that fills your training all year round

You already have low-ticket products, so the class itself should be free. A practitioner toolkit built from your book Anxiety: The Missing Stage of Grief sits on the thank-you page, it earns from day one and helps pay for the ads, and the replay page sends the serious ones to an application for your next Grief & Loss Training cohort.

Live masterclass

Is this you?

Grief walks into your sessions. Your training barely mentioned it.

  • A client brings up a loss and you’re not sure whether to go toward it or give it space.
  • You learned the five stages, and the people in front of you don’t follow them.
  • You see worry, panic or sleeplessness after a death and wonder how much of it is grief.
  • You’d like to make grief part of your practice, but you want to do it well.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover in one hour

Why the five stages fall short

Where the classic model came from, what it was never meant to do, and a more honest picture of how grief moves.

Anxiety, the missing stage

How anxiety shows up after a loss, why it’s so often missed, and what that means for the way you hold a session.

Conscious grieving

The framework from my book: helping people engage with their grief actively instead of waiting for time to do the work.

The first conversation

What to say, what to ask and what to leave alone when someone first tells you about a loss.

Taking care of yourself

Grief work is heavy. How to keep showing up for it without carrying it all home.

Meet Claire

Hi, I’m Claire Bidwell Smith

Grief therapist and bestselling author.

I’m a grief therapist (LCPC) and the author of five books, including Conscious Grieving, Anxious Grief and Anxiety: The Missing Stage of Grief. My work has been featured in the New York Times, on NPR and CNN, and with Oprah and Goop.

Through my Grief & Loss Training I teach therapists, coaches and other professionals how to support people through loss. This free class is where I share the foundations.

Questions

Before you save your seat

Who is this class for?

Therapists, counsellors, social workers, coaches, chaplains, hospice and end-of-life workers: anyone whose work brings them close to people who are grieving.

Do I need to be a licensed clinician?

No. The class is educational and open to any helping professional.

What if I can’t make it live?

Sign up anyway. Everyone who registers gets the replay.

Is it really free?

Yes. Come, take notes, bring your questions, and decide afterwards whether you want to go deeper.

That’s why I built the Grief & Loss Training: six weeks live, real interventions you can use with clients, and a community of people doing the same work.

Script 1 · “The five stages”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“If you work with people, you were probably taught the five stages of grief. Here’s what they leave out.”

Body

“I’ve spent my career as a grief therapist and written five books on loss. The people in front of you rarely move in neat stages. In my free class I’ll show you a more honest picture, and what to do with it in session.”

CTA

“Join me live for Beyond the Five Stages. It’s free for helping professionals. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: calm talking to camera, warm low light, cream captions on charcoal.

Script 2 · “The missing stage”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“There’s a part of grief most training never mentions.”

Body

“It’s anxiety. Worry, restlessness, a sense that something else will go wrong. I wrote a book about it because I kept seeing it missed. In this free hour I’ll show you how to recognise it and talk about it with clients.”

CTA

“The class is free and the replay is included. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: at your desk with your books in frame, one on-screen card: “Anxiety: the missing stage.”

Script 3 · “The first conversation”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“A client tells you about a loss. What do you say next?”

Body

“For a lot of therapists and coaches, that moment feels uncertain. Go toward it? Give it space? In my free masterclass I’ll walk you through the first conversation, step by step.”

CTA

“Join me live in Beyond the Five Stages. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: seated, two-camera interview style, with three text cards: Ask · Listen · Leave alone.

All ads speak to professionals about their clients, never to the viewer about a loss of their own. Educational content, not medical advice.
